type: Compiled family-tree chart (image; derivative source, author unknown)
title: Family-tree chart of the Javor family, a watermarked preview, undated
extract: A printed family-tree chart, in colour, titled 'Rodostrom rodiny Javorovej' (family tree of the Javor family), with the word 'náhľad' (preview) stamped across it several times. About 250 name boxes in eight or nine generations, a coat of arms, eleven photographs and two churches. At this size only the lowest three generations and the photograph captions can be read at all. No Duska is legible anywhere on it. One ancestor is legible in part: Mary D[an]ko or D[em]ko, born 1906, died 1991, whose box appears to give a birthplace in the U.S.A. and a line naming Vysoká nad Uhom. Her parents' boxes read Andrej D[..]ko and Mária M[...]ová, both with Vysoká nad Uhom. The younger generations are living people and are not abstracted here.
reliability: Derivative and unsourced: a designer's chart with no citations, seen as a small preview image. Most of it cannot be read. Nothing on it is evidence for the Duska line.

type: Parish register, opening page (image)
title: First page of the Senné register volume: 'Memoria digna', the list of parish priests from 1718
extract: 'Worth remembering. The series of parish priests of the church of Szenna, as far as it could be dug out of old documents, the registers especially, after the church was recovered from the Calvinists in 1718.' Twenty-six priests follow, from Adamus Petrik to Georgius Balás (1850 to 1886), among them Stephanus Rácz, 1831 to 1841. Under Balás: windows repaired, a new organ bought; on 28 October 1865 at eleven at night something was destroyed by fire 'through a malicious man'; a bell was blessed on 20 July 1871 by Bishop László Bíró in honour of St Ladislaus, with a bell for Solymos dedicated to St Christopher. Then, in later hands: Julius Buzinkay made interim administrator; Stephanus Rusznák named administrator on 4 October 1886, invested 1887, died 3 May 1892; Buzinkay took the place on 24 July 1892 and was invested on 7 November 1894. The image carries a microfilm target reading 'Whole Volume'. Much of the lower half is at the limit of legibility and is given only in outline.
reliability: Original record, image copy. Years in square brackets come from the owner's file name, which is a label and not evidence. Reading level: medium.

type: Newspaper report (derivative source, printed far from the event), as a print from a newspaper archive
title: Newspaper report of an explosion at Niobrara, Nebraska, that killed an Annie Duska, January 1911
extract: A one-page print of a clipping from an Ohio newspaper, the Telegraph-Forum of Bucyrus, 17 January 1911, page 4, read in full at B-026. A report from Niobrara, Nebraska, dated 16 January: the gas lighting plant of the Hubbard hotel exploded and killed M. W. Kimball, Annie Duska, Kenneth Kindall and R. F. Crosby; four women were rescued from the fire, which burned the hotel. Nothing in it says where she came from, how old she was or whose kin she was. A Nebraska paper of the same week names the hotel's owner as Michael Kendall and lists among the dead 'Ann Duseka, a cook' (lead L-021), so the Ohio wire copy garbled at least one name and her surname is spelled two ways. The file is held because its footer carries the owner's account name on the newspaper site; the report itself is transcribed here whole.
reliability: A wire report reprinted in another state, with at least one name garbled (Kimball for Kendall). Reading level: high.

type: Printed map (published source)
title: Map of Ung county by Pál Gönczy, [1890s]
extract: A printed colour map of Ung county, drawn by Pál Gönczy, at 1:380,000, with relief, rivers, marsh, roads, the railway and the four districts outlined in red. It gives the county's area as 3,052.84 square kilometres and its population as 135,247, which dates it to the 1890s. For this archive it shows three things. Solymos and Szenna are neighbours, about 4 km apart by the map's scale, with marsh between them. The red district line runs between them: Solymos, Jesztreb, Rebrin and Gézsény lie in the Szobránc district, and Szenna, Pályin, Viszoka and Csicser in the Kapos district. And Lasztomér, the home of the carpenter János Demko's wife, lies just over the county line in Zemplén. Any record kept by district, a census among them, will have the two villages in different bundles.
reliability: A published map; good for places, names in use and district lines at its date. The coloured squares on the second map are a later addition with no key.

type: Printed map (published source)
title: Map of Ung county of 1915 with a coloured square added on each village
extract: A black-and-white school map of Ung county issued for the minister of religion and education, dated 1915 in the corner, with the population of 1910 (162,089) and six districts. Someone has since added a small coloured square on every village: red across the south around Nagykapos and Csap, green across the west around Szobránc, purple through the mountains and the east, a few striped or dotted. The image has no key to the colours; by where they fall they look like the main language of each village (Hungarian, Slovak, Ruthenian), and that is this agent's inference, not something the map says. Solymos, Ungszenna, Rebrény, Gézsény and Magasrév are green; Csicser is red. Two names matter here. Szenna is 'Ungszenna', the form the Senné register takes up between 1903 and 1906. And where the older map has Viszoka, this one has Magasrév: the birthplace written on the Demko agent's 1906 record is Viszoka under its new name.
reliability: A published map; good for places, names in use and district lines at its date. The coloured squares on the second map are a later addition with no key.

type: Statistical return of marriage to the Québec government (original, made at the ceremony; not the act of marriage)
title: Québec declaration of marriage, 11 October 1984: Kevin Duska and Lyne Lefebvre
extract: A typed and signed Québec government form, the declaration of a civil marriage. On 11 October 1984, at the Palais de Justice in Montréal, Kevin Duska, single, born in Montréal in 1962, married Lyne Lefebvre, single, born in Montréal on 4 July 1964, French-speaking. The groom's father is entered as Steve Duska, born in Czechoslovakia, and Steve J. Duska signs as a witness. This is the first document in the archive for the link between Kevin's father and his grandfather Štefan. The bride was Kevin's mother; he states that she has died, so her name and the marriage are shown (S-000-10). Still withheld, and blacked out on the published copy: the groom's day and month of birth, the couple's address and the groom's signature, because Kevin does not know whether his father is living; the bride's parents and the groom's mother, who belong to lines outside this experiment and whose status is not known; the second witness; and the official.
reliability: Typed, with signatures; made at the event by the parties. Reading level: high. Published in part: see the document.

type: Government letter (original)
title: Letter of the Immigration Branch, Ottawa, to Mike Duska, 11 Sep 1937
extract: A typed letter from the Canadian immigration service in Ottawa to Mike Duska at 1196a St. George Street, Montréal. He had applied for his wife Maria, 'aged 28', and son Stefan, aged 7, of Iňačovce, to be admitted to Canada, and the letter says the entry letter has gone to the Canadian Pacific agent at Windsor Station. So Michal Duska was settled in Montréal by September 1937 and sent for his family. The owner's file name calls this a citizenship application; it is an admission letter. Maria was in fact 31. The letter gives no age or birthplace for Mike himself.
reliability: Typed original. The ages in it are as the applicant gave them; the wife's is three years out. The pile is the sorter's label and is not evidence. Custody: found by the owner among his grandfather's papers (S-000-9).

type: Steamship company receipt (original)
title: Canadian Pacific Steamships receipt no. 242299, Montréal, 17 Sep 1937
extract: The purchaser's copy of a prepaid passage order. On 17 September 1937, in Montréal, Mr. Mike Duska of 1196a St. George Street paid $178.50 for a third-class ocean passage from Prague to a Canadian port for Mrs. Maria Duska, an adult, and Master Stefan Duska, aged 7, of Iňačovce. It was bought six days after the immigration letter.
reliability: Typed original. The pile is the sorter's label and is not evidence. Custody: found by the owner among his grandfather's papers (S-000-9).

type: Court consent, printed form typed in (original)
title: Guardianship consent, district court of Michalovce, Nsl 446/37, 7 Oct 1937
extract: A printed court form, typed in. The district court at Michalovce, acting as guardianship office, file Nsl 446/37, consents on 7 October 1937 that the minor Štefan Duško, born 23 October 1929 at Senné, may emigrate in the company of his mother, Mária Dušková née Demková of Iňačovce, to Canada, to his father Michal Duško. The mother may sign the transport contract in the guardian's place. The reasons: the father asked for it, the boy will be fully provided for with him, and the escort is over 24 years old, wholly reliable, and has bound herself in writing to take him all the way. The surname is typed Duško throughout. The boy's birthday is given as 23 October; the parish certificate of 1947 has 21 October. Nothing is said of the father's age or of where in Canada he was.
reliability: Sealed original; some typing faint. It gives the boy's birthday as 23 October, against 21 October in the parish certificate of 1947. The pile is the sorter's label and is not evidence. Custody: found by the owner among his grandfather's papers (S-000-9).

type: Transport contract (original, photograph cropped)
title: Canadian Pacific transport contract no. 15621, Prague, 8 Nov 1937
extract: The emigrant's contract with the Canadian Pacific office in Prague, no. 15621, emigration register nos. 487 and 488. Maria Dušková, 31, married, a farm worker, Czechoslovak, last living at Iňačovce, and Štefan Duška, 8, single, are to go third class by train from Prague on 8 November 1937 and by the ship Montrose from Antwerp on 11 November 1937 to Montréal. The fare is marked as paid in Canada; she paid 20 crowns of insurance on 6 November, and signs 'Marja Duskova'. The public copy of this image is cropped on the right, where an envelope bearing another person's name lay beside the sheet.
reliability: Handwritten on a printed form; reading level medium. The pile is the sorter's label and is not evidence. Custody: found by the owner among his grandfather's papers (S-000-9).

type: Census household sheet (original record, screen capture)
title: Census of 1930, Beša, house 1[0]4: the household of Ignác Schwarcz
extract: A household sheet of the Czechoslovak census of 1930, printed in Slovak and Hungarian and filled in in Hungarian: Beša, district of Veľké Kapušany, house 1[0]4, owner Ignác Schwarcz, for the night of 1 to 2 December 1930. Seven people, three generations. Ignác Schwarcz, house owner, born 2 March 1865, married, a merchant on his own account, in the village since January 1870. Fanny, his wife, born 8 August 1868, married in September 1886, mother of eight children of whom two are entered beside it. Lipót, their son, born 1 January 1888, married, a merchant. Hermin, their daughter-in-law, born 21 September 1894, married on 6 January 1920 and in the village from that day. The grandchildren Vilmos (8 March 1921), Edit (6 December 192[3]) and Tibor (6 October 1926). All are Czechoslovak citizens with their home commune at Beša; nationality is entered as Jewish and religion as Israelite; the adults read and write. There is no Duska and no Demko on the sheet. The owner's file is numbered 1 and his folder is called 'whole', so this is all he kept from Beša. The only Schwarz in this archive is Erzsébet Schwarz of Alsó-Ribnicze, the Catholic wife of György Duska the younger of Senné; nothing on this sheet connects the two.
reliability: Dates of birth as the household gave them to the enumerator. Reading level: medium; the image is small. The owner's file name reads the head's given name as 'Igure'; the sheet has Ignác.

title: Census of 1930, Senné, house 145: Andrej Duška, his wife Anna, their daughter-in-law Maria and grandson Štefan
extract: House 145, owner Andrej Duška, on the night of 1 to 2 December 1930. Andrej Duška, head, born 24 November 1868 at Senné, married, a farm day-labourer who can neither read nor write. Anna, his wife, born 24 August 1872 at Senné, married on 18 January 1892, mother of twelve children of whom nine are living; she can read. Juraj, their son, born 2 March 1910, single, a day-labourer. Maria Dušková, 'daughter-in-law of the head', born 15 August 1907 at Iňačovce, Greek Catholic, married on 30 January 1927 and living in Senné since that day. Štefan Duška, 'grandson', born 23 October 1929 at Senné, Roman Catholic. Maria's husband is not in the house. This is the record that names Michal Duska's parents. Štefan, born 23 October 1929, son of a Greek Catholic Maria from Iňačovce, is the Štefan of the 1937 passport and court consent, whose father was Michal. He is entered as the grandson, and his mother as the daughter-in-law, of Andrej and Anna, married 18 January 1892: the András Duska and Anna Nyemcsik of the marriage entry D-006-03, whose son Mihály was baptised on 3 July 1903 (D-009-79). Maria's date of birth here, 15 August 1907, differs from her passport's 22 August 1906; her father-in-law, who could not read, was probably the informant.
reliability: Dates as the household told the enumerator; a head who could not read may be a year out on a daughter-in-law. Reading level: medium. The owner's file name is a label and is not evidence.

type: Passenger list (original record, cropped image)
title: Passenger list: Mikulas Duska, 39, and Michal Duska, 26, of Senné, arriving in Canada, [1929 or 1930]
extract: An enlarged crop of a typed passenger list of men arriving in Canada, with later notes by the immigration office. Three men in a row are from Senné, Czechoslovakia, Slovak: Andrey Dzvonik, 24; Mikulas Duska, 39; and Michal Duska, 26. The ship, the port and the date are not in the crop. Against Michal an office hand has written 'Copy on O.F. 633695' and 'Nat. 22/4/40': a copy of the entry went to file 633695, and he was naturalised on 22 April 1940. That file number is the one on the Immigration Branch letter of 1937 to Mike Duska of Montréal (D-006-11, read there as 6336[93]), so this Michal is Štefan's father. Against Mikulas: 'Nat: 21/1/46'. Between the two lines a hand has written what looks like '+ Brother'; the typed relationship column has only ditto marks under 'none'. The ages date the voyage: a man born on 3 July 1903 was 26 until July 1930, and one born on 28 November 1890 was 39 from November 1929, so they sailed between late November 1929 and early July 1930, within months of Štefan's birth. A Michal born in December 1896 would have been 33.
reliability: Typed at the time from the passengers' papers; ages are as declared. The ink notes are later office work. Reading level: medium; the word read 'Brother' is doubtful.

type: Census household sheets, names only (original records, redacted by the publishing archive; screen captures)
title: Senné in the census of 1940: houses 11, 14 and 73, and one sheet from another Senné
extract: The Slovak census of 15 December 1940 for Senné, now in the Michalovce district, as the portal shows it: the forms are public only down the left edge, with the surnames and given names, and every other column is blacked out. What the names alone give: at house 11, Mária Dušková née Hankoščáková with Anna and Mária, and on the back, among those away from home, Mikuláš Duška; at house 14, Mária Dušková née Feigerle [?], alone; at house 73, Jozef Duška and Anna née Chalahánová, a second Jozef with a wife Anna, a married daughter, and three more Duškas. The maiden name at house 11 matters. The cemetery record D-006-09 names the spouse of 'Mikalis' Duska as 'Hancosek': the same surname, worn down by a French clerk. Her given name there is Anna and here it is Mária. No sheet for house 145 is in the folder.
reliability: Names as written by the enumerator. Nothing else on the sheets can be seen. Slovak National Archive, census of 1940, box 915 (box 547 for the other Senné). Reading level: medium.

type: Newspaper death notice (derivative, supplied by the family; print from a newspaper archive)
title: Death notice of Mike Duska, Sr., The Montreal Star, 2 February 1974
extract: A death notice from The Montreal Star of Saturday 2 February 1974, page 10. Mike Duska, Sr., died at the Montreal General Hospital on 31 January 1974, aged 71. He was the husband of the late Mary Demko, the father of Steve and Mike, and the grandfather of Kevin. The funeral was on Monday 4 February from the Slovak church of St. Cyril and Method, with burial in Côte-des-Neiges cemetery, where his wife's stone stands. This is Michal Duska, Ahn 8. A man born on 3 July 1903 was 70, not 71, on that day; a family's count a year out is ordinary. The notice shows a second son, Mike, not met in any earlier record; he was not on his mother's passport in 1937, so he was born in Canada after that. The 'Sr.' is for him. The page as the owner saved it prints his account name on a newspaper website and is not published; the notice itself is shown as a crop.
reliability: The pile is the sorter's label and is not evidence. Reading level: high.

type: Parish extract of a baptism entry (derivative, sealed)
title: Baptismal certificate of Štefan Duška, issued at Senné on 1 October 1955
extract: A second extract of the same register entry as the certificate of 1947 (D-X01-01): Senné Roman Catholic baptisms, volume IV, page 110, entry 43 of 1929. Štefan, born 21 October 1929, baptised 26 October, legitimate son of Michal Duška, cottar, Roman Catholic, of Senné, and Mária Demko, Greek Catholic, of Iňačovce; parents' home Senné 160; godparents Jozef Macko-Kocák, student, Greek Catholic, of Michalovce, and Zuzanna Bandura née Hankoščák, Roman Catholic, of Senné; baptised by Ján Barna, parish priest. Issued at Senné on 1 October 1955, eight weeks before Štefan's wedding in Montréal. Two things it settles: the church's date is 21 October, written by two priests eight years apart, against the 23rd of the civil papers; and the godmother is clearly Zuzanna, born Hankoščák, the family of Mikuláš Duška's wife.
reliability: The pile is the sorter's label and is not evidence. Reading level: high.

type: Statistical return of marriage to the Québec government (original, made at the ceremony; not the act of marriage)
title: Québec registration of the marriage of Michael Duska, born 1 December 1938, Montréal, 8 December 1973
extract: The provincial registration of a marriage at the church of St-Alphonse d'Youville, Montréal, on 8 December 1973, after banns. The groom is Michael Duska, inspection manager, single, 35, born in Montréal on 1 December 1938, Roman Catholic, a Canadian citizen. The bride is Marie-Claire-Francine Quenneville, born in 1949; her status is not known, so she is given by name and year only and the image is held. The owner states that the groom, his great-uncle 'Mike Jr', has died (S-000-12). A boy born in Montréal on 1 December 1938 fits a couple reunited there in November 1937, and eight weeks after this wedding the death notice of Mike Duska, Sr., names a son Mike. One thing on the form is wrong on any reading: the groom's ethnic origin is typed 'Indou' and his father's birthplace 'Inde', Hindu and India. His father was born at Senné. That he is the son of Michal Duska and Maria Demko is held at 75 in 100 (H-071): the form does not name his parents.
reliability: Typed at the time from the parties' statements, with one plain clerical error (the groom's origin and his father's birthplace). Reading level: high.

type: Cemetery correspondence (the cemetery's own statement)
title: Message from Notre-Dame-des-Neiges cemetery to the owner: section FT 01965 is a common grave, and three Duskas are on its books
extract: The cemetery writes, unsigned: 'I have sent you all the information we had on the Duskas buried in our cemetery. We have only three on record. Section FT 01965 is a common grave. The FT, temporary graves, were common graves. The dead were buried side by side in the order they reached the cemetery. The lot number is the year of arrival. Mikalis Duska arrived on 28 November 1965 and was buried in the common graves: hence FT 01965. Nothing links the dead of one concession but the year of death, and there are more than 1,000 a year for those years. I cannot give you those lists. As for dates of birth and death, before the 1980s and 1990s cemeteries recorded almost none; the parish of the funeral kept the fuller register.' The footer gives the cemetery's own web address. Three things follow. The earlier printout (D-006-09) was sent to the owner by the cemetery. Plot '1965' is not a coincidence with the year. And the cemetery says it kept almost no dates of birth then, which puts a question against the birth date on its printout (see H-060).
reliability: Reading level: high (typed text).

type: Obituary (written by the grandson, the owner of this archive)
title: Obituary of Stefan 'Steve' Duska, died Montréal 6 June 2018, written by his grandson, the owner of this archive
extract: Stefan 'Steve' Duska died in Montréal on Wednesday 6 June 2018, aged 88. He was the son of Michal and Maria (Demko), was born at Senné, came to Canada 'in early childhood', and retired from the postal service. His wife Joan (Leonard) died before him. He was father to Kevin, grandfather to Kevin Jr., whom he and his wife raised, and brother to Mike. Funeral mass on Wednesday 27 June 2018 at St-Brendan's, 3542 Rosemont Boulevard, Montréal; the remains to be interred afterwards at Notre-Dame-des-Neiges. The heading gives his birth as 21 September 1929. Every record made in his lifetime says October: the 21st in the parish book and on his marriage form, the 23rd on the papers of 1937. The owner wrote the obituary and says September is his own slip (S-000-19). Every relationship in the text was already in this tree from records before it was read; what is new is the day of death, the funeral, the cemetery, that his wife died first, and that his brother was living in June 2018.
reliability: Written within three weeks of the death by the man's grandson, who was raised by him: firsthand for the death, the funeral and the household, hearsay for the birth and the parents. Not independent of the owner. One date in it is wrong by his own account. Reading level: high.

Maria Demko was 31; the first digit of her age is blurred on the film and looks more like a 5. They share a page, as a mother and child on one passport would. The index names no ship, port or day. The other names on the sheet are strangers: Durston, Durway, Dussault, Dussean, four Duszeneks and three Duthies.

type: Online index to deaths (derivative)
title: Index to Québec deaths: Michael Duska, died 31 January 1974, and Mikalis Duska, died 28 November 1965
extract: DUSKA, MICHAEL. Sex M. Status V [widower]. Date of birth 2-7-1903. Age 70. Residence Montréal. Father: DUSKA, Joseph. Mother: ', E.' Spouse: DEMKO. Date of death 31-1-1974. This is Ahn 8 by the death date, the age and the wife. Two things do not fit the registers: the birth is a day early (the baptism book has 3 July), and the father is 'Joseph' where the baptism of 1903, the census of 1930 and the marriage of 1892 all have András. The parents of a man of 70 were told to the registrar by whoever reported the death (H-093). DUSKA, MIKALIS. Sex M. Status V [widower]. Date of birth 28-11-1890. Age 75. Residence Montréal. Date of death 28-11-1965. No parents and no spouse. The cemetery's record has the same birth date and the same day as the day it received him (D-006-09). Here the day is called the date of death. So a second set of books, the civil one, holds the birth date of 28 November 1890, which is the day Miklós Duska was born at Szenna 6 (D-015-07). By this index he died on his seventy-fifth birthday and was a widower.
reliability: A database entry; the registrations behind it are not seen. The dates are sound where they can be checked. The parents in the first entry are wrong against three original records. Reading level: high.

type: Civil birth certificate (official extract of 2005 from the register of 1929)
title: Birth certificate of Štefan Duška from the civil register: born 23 October 1929 at Senné; issued at Palín, 5 May 2005
extract: The Slovak Republic's birth certificate, on security paper, no. 31/2005. In the book of births of the registry office, volume 5, year 1929, page 102, entry 57, is written: born 23 October 1929 at Senné, Štefan Duška, a boy. Father: Michal Duška, 26 years old. Mother: Mária Demková, 23 years old. Birth numbers, dates and places of birth of the parents and citizenship: 'neuvedené', not stated. No remarks. Issued at Palín on 5 May 2005 under the seal of the commune's registry office. This is the state's book, and it says the 23rd. The parish's book says the 21st (D-X01-01). The parents' ages fit Michal born July 1903 and Maria born August 1906. Štefan was 75 and living in Montréal when it was issued.

extract: Michael Walter Duska, 1938 to 2019, died on 14 June 2019. Husband of a second wife, who survives him. 'Predeceased by his parents, Michal Duska and Maria Demo, as well as his brother Steve and sister-in-law Joan.' He leaves a son, two stepchildren and two grandchildren, 'as well as family in Slovakia and the Philippines'. He helped found a company called Theocon; he wintered in Florida and golfed. No place of death, burial or funeral home. The mother's surname has lost its k. With the index card of his first marriage (D-015-10) this closes H-071: the Michael born in Montréal on 1 December 1938 is the younger son of Ahn 8 and Ahn 9, and he outlived his brother Štefan by a year and eight days.
reliability: A family-written notice printed eight days after the death: firsthand for the death and the household, hearsay for the parents, whose names it gives with one letter lost. Read from the owner's paste. Reading level: high.

type: Raw genotype export, compared with another (this agent's computation)
title: Raw AncestryDNA data of a kit the owner calls Steve's, and its comparison with the owner's
extract: Laid beside the owner's own AncestryDNA file (D-016-16), same array, 636,861 autosomal markers read in both. Same genotype at 63.37 per cent, one allele in common at 33.25, opposite homozygotes at 3.38 (21,521 markers), so not parent and child and not one person. Eighteen stretches of at least 7 megabases where the two share one copy throughout, 1,106 Mb of the 2,791 Mb the markers span: 39.6 per cent of the length of the autosomes, which is 19.8 per cent of the grandson's DNA. Chromosomes 10, 20 and 22 are shared from end to end; 3, 5, 7, 8, 9 and 21 not at all. X chromosome: 28,789 markers, 76.8 per cent alike by chance and no long run: nothing shared, as a male line requires. Y chromosome: 1,638 markers read in both, 1,638 identical. Mitochondrial: 195 of 195 alike, which on so few and such common markers decides nothing.
reliability: Two primary data files and a comparison anyone can repeat from them. The method is a plain one: stretches with no opposing homozygotes, 7 Mb and 700 markers at least. Lengths are in megabases; no genetic map was to hand, so no centimorgan figure is claimed. Whose file it is rests on the owner's label and on the result itself. Reading level: not applicable.

type: DNA match list (derivative of the tests; a database's computation)
title: GEDmatch one-to-many match list for the kit named Stefan Duska (KJ4…), 3,000 matches
extract: GEDmatch 'One-to-Many' for the kit beginning KJ4, which the site itself heads 'matches 1:3000 for Stefan Duska': the name is on the kit, not only on the owner's file. The first 3,000 matches, the weakest at 10.2 cM. The top four are the owner's own four kits, at 1,553 to 1,559 cM in total, largest piece 125 to 150 cM, 'generations 1.6', nothing on X: the site's own measure of the grandfather and grandson link (H-097). After them there is no near relative at all. One match at 52 cM, four between 35 and 50, 44 between 25 and 35, 89 between 20 and 25, 315 between 15 and 20, and 2,543 between 10 and 15. Not one of the 2,996 other kits carries the surname Duska in any spelling, nor Demko, Krak, Nyemcsik, Hresko, Kocsis or Schwarz. Many of the surnames near the top are of Carpathian make, Slovak, Rusyn, Polish or Hungarian, on kits tested in North America: the descendants of other emigrants from the same hills. The page's footer reads 'Copyright 2026': it was copied this year, not in 2022.
reliability: A testing database's measure of shared DNA between one kit and thousands of others. Sound for the amounts. A name on a kit is whatever its owner typed. It finds relatives; it does not say how they are related. Reading level: high.
